# Results — Study 859 (Return-on-Invested-Capital Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **ROIC
(NOPAT / invested capital) is a cleaner, unlevered quality gauge than ROE and sorts future
returns**, and does it **add anything over plain ROE (200) / gross profitability (122)** on a
survivor mega-cap panel? Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. Stamped as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Prices Fingerprint `030498da471a` (yfinance daily adjusted closes);
events cache = 844 (ticker, filing) rows.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **44** large US **non-financial** filers (fixed, current survivors); **32** produced a valid ROIC (others lack quarterly `OperatingIncomeLoss` / long-term debt on EDGAR) |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: `OperatingIncomeLoss` (→ trailing-twelve-month NOPAT), `StockholdersEquity`, `LongTermDebtNoncurrent`, `CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue`; de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **844** balance-sheet quarters, period ends **2009-06-27 → 2026-05-29**, each stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 44 names, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `roic` = TTM NOPAT ÷ (LongTermDebt + Equity − Cash); NOPAT = OperatingIncome × (1 − 0.21) |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh signals into **terciles**, long top / short bottom, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Tax-rate invariance.** NOPAT applies a flat 21% haircut to operating income. Because that
`(1 − 0.21)` scalar is common to every name, it does **not** change the cross-sectional ROIC
ranking — only the printed ROIC magnitude — so every long-short number below is invariant to the
tax assumption (proved in the test-suite).

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** The monthly cross-section grows from single digits in 2009-11
to ≈20 by the mid-2020s (avg **16.5**). XBRL only begins ~2009-2010 and several names
re-registered under new CIKs after reorgs (XOM 2024, DIS 2019, LIN 2018), truncating machine-
readable history. Terciles on a thin cross-section are noisy by construction. **Survivorship** is
named on the Signal axis: the basket is current survivors, so the low-ROIC **short** leg cannot
hold the capital-destroyers that were acquired or delisted — any short-side edge is an upper bound.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does ROIC sort returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `roic` level, one execution lag, 2009-09 → 2026-06
(**202 months**, avg cross-section 16.5 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **+13.5 bps/month** (+1.62%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | +0.48 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **+0.40** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | 0.12 |
| monthly hit rate | 50% |
| long leg / short leg | +179.3 / +165.8 bps/month |
| turnover (one-way, monthly) | 0.06 |

The point estimate is **right-signed but economically trivial (~+1.6%/yr gross) and
statistically indistinguishable from zero** (NW *t* = +0.40, one-sample +0.48). The two "best"
specifications still fall far short: a staleness-120 cut is **+37.2 bps, NW *t* = +1.12**, and the
ROIC-**change** variant (`roic_chg`) is **+32.1 bps, NW *t* = +1.14** (Sharpe 0.28). Nothing
approaches the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by ROIC)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `roic`; top-minus-bottom forward drift, entered one day
after the filing:

| horizon | n | top | bottom | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 840 | +1.23% | +0.96% | **+0.27%** | +0.47 | 50% | 0.31 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 818 | +4.94% | +4.58% | **+0.37%** | +0.29 | 51% | 0.36 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 811 | +8.37% | +10.05% | **−1.68%** | −0.85 | 51% | 0.82 |

Flat, and **worse than flat at the 2-quarter horizon**, where high-ROIC names actually
*under*-return low-ROIC names by −1.68%. The 63-day terciles are **non-monotone** (+4.58% /
+5.00% / +4.94% low→high), the long-short *t* never exceeds +0.47, and the label-shuffle placebo
*p* sits at 0.3-0.8 — a random tercile split beats the real one a third to four-fifths of the
time. There is **no forward-return sort** in ROIC on this tape.

## Era split — and the sign flips

Calendar long-short, split at 2018-01-01 (the TCJA statutory-rate change):

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2009-2017 | 100 | **−5.6 bps** | −0.14 |
| 2018-2026 | 102 | **+32.2 bps** | +0.60 |

The tiny full-sample positive is entirely a **post-2018** artefact; pre-2018 the sign is
*negative*. Neither era clears the bar, and a signal whose sign flips across the sample is the
opposite of robust.

## Third axis — does ROIC add anything over ROE (200) / gross profitability (122)?

The *same* calendar long-short, run on each quality signal over the identical panel:

| signal | long-short | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe | months |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ROIC** (this study) | +13.5 bps/mo | **+0.40** | 0.12 | 202 |
| ROIC change | +32.1 bps/mo | +1.14 | 0.28 | 189 |
| **ROE** (200) | **−65.5 bps/mo** | **−1.36** | −0.50 | 89 |
| **Gross profitability** (122) | **−164.1 bps/mo** | **−1.59** | −0.85 | 60 |

ROIC↔ROE cross-sectional **rank correlation = +0.75**. The verdict on the headline question:
**ROIC adds essentially nothing you can certify** — but the *reason* is the interesting part. On
this **survivor mega-cap** panel **none** of the classic quality signals earn a premium; ROIC is
merely the *least bad*, the only one that stays right-signed, while plain ROE and gross
profitability come out **negative** (wrong-signed, though also insignificant on their thinner
sub-panels). And because ROIC and ROE rank +0.75 together, ROIC is largely the same bet with the
leverage scrubbed off. The quality premium the literature documents evidently lives in the
smaller, "junkier" cross-section that a mega-cap survivor basket excludes by construction.

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.06, a slow balance-sheet signal):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | +8.1 bps/mo | +0.98%/yr | +0.24 | 0.07 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | +2.8 bps/mo | +0.33%/yr | +0.08 | 0.02 |

Costs are almost irrelevant (turnover is tiny), but so is the edge: net NW *t* = +0.08, Sharpe
0.02. You cannot be paid for a spread that was zero before costs.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + signal panel with a TUNABLE planted premium (high-ROIC names drift up); no
network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **−0.38** (sd 1.43), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **2/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 859) | **+23.63** (mean +825.4 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null and lights up violently on a planted premium. (Two of twelve
HAC *t*'s cross \|2\| on the null — a little rich, but with sd 1.43 over ~180-month synthetic
series it is within noise, and the real-tape *t* = +0.40 is nowhere near either way.) The
machinery is unbiased and powered, so the real-tape near-zero is a genuine null, not a broken
pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** ROIC does **not** sort returns on this panel. The primary tercile long-short
  is a near-perfect null (**+13.5 bps/mo, NW *t* = +0.40**, one-sample +0.48); the best
  specifications (staleness-120 +1.12, ROIC-change +1.14) still don't approach 2; the pooled event
  drift is **flat and turns negative at 2 quarters** (−1.68%, non-monotone terciles, placebo
  *p* ≈ 0.4-0.8); and the era split **flips sign** (−5.6 bps pre-2018, +32.2 bps after). Right-
  signed by a hair, real by no measure.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of 20 bps + 100 bps borrow: +0.33%/yr, NW *t* = +0.08, Sharpe
  0.02. Nothing to trade — it fails before costs.
- **Does ROIC add anything over ROE / gross profitability? — NO (immaterial).** On this survivor
  mega-cap panel none of the quality signals certify; ROIC is only the least bad (the sole one
  that stays right-signed, ROE −1.36 and GP −1.59 going *negative*), and it ranks +0.75 with ROE
  — largely the same bet, leverage removed. The unlevered refinement buys no certifiable edge
  here; the quality premium lives in the junkier cross-section a mega-cap survivor basket omits.
